$description:
Card component tokens (pulled ahead of its W7 catalog slot per demo-app GAP #1 — every settings-page section had to fall back to Stack+Divider with no bordered/elevated container available). D-008 is the single most important constraint here: 'ห้ามมี drop-shadow ตกแต่งบน card/button/input ปกติ ... shadow สงวนไว้เฉพาะ layer ที่ต้อง ลอยจริง เท่านั้น (modal, popover, toast)' — Card sits IN the page flow next to other content, it never floats above it, so this file has zero shadow.* references, unlike dialog.json/popover.json/toast.json which legitimately use shadow.elevation.*.

FIXED (post-batch review, before v0.1.0 publish): `root.border` was originally `border.hairline`, matching Divider/Fieldset — but those two are a DIFFERENT category (a bare rule line and an unfilled `<fieldset>` respectively; neither has its own background, so the border genuinely is their only visual mechanism and citing them as precedent for Card was wrong). Card DOES have its own fill (`surface.raised`), so the real question is whether that fill alone separates it from the page — checked both mathematically (surface.raised vs surface.canvas = 1.06:1 both themes, i.e. imperceptible) and visually (real Storybook screenshot: on its own, the fill is not visible at all — only the border reads). Since neither the fill nor `border.hairline` (1.51:1 light / 1.24:1 dark on surface.canvas) clears WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 non-text-contrast minimum, and the border IS the only boundary cue in practice, this was a real accessibility failure, not an acceptable decorative-hairline case — E-001 explicitly excludes border/divider/focus-ring/input-edge from its scope, so it could not have been cited either. Switched `root.border` to `color.border.interactive` (the same token Button outline/Input/Checkbox/Radio/RadioCards already rely on for their own real interactive/panel boundaries per D-014) — measures 3.72:1 (light) / 3.72:1 (dark) against `surface.canvas`, both clearing 3:1. `header`/`footer` borders stay on `border.hairline` deliberately: those are internal quiet dividers *within* an already-established card region (same category as a Divider placed inside a panel), not the card's own outer boundary against the page — WCAG 1.4.11 doesn't apply to them the way it applies to the root edge.

Contrast self-check (relative-luminance formula against packages/tokens/build/css/{light,dark}.css resolved hex, both themes):
- text.default on surface.raised: light #282623/#f8f6f4 = 14.00:1, dark #f2efeb/#282623 = 13.16:1 (>>4.5:1)
- text.subtle (footer/meta) on surface.raised: light #615d57/#f8f6f4 = 6.07:1, dark neutral.300 #bbb7b0/#282623 = 8.06:1 (>>4.5:1)
- root.border (border.interactive, the card's own outer boundary) on surface.canvas: light neutral.500 #7e7a74/#f2efeb = 3.72:1, dark #7e7a74/#242220 = 3.72:1 (both clear 3:1 — real fix, not an exception)
- header/footer internal divider (border.hairline) on surface.raised: light 1.40:1, dark 1.18:1 — expected and correct for an internal quiet divider, not a boundary
- border.interactive (clickable card hover/focus-visible ring) on surface.raised: light 3.96:1, dark 3.54:1 (clears 3:1 — same as root.border now, so hover no longer changes contrast class, just shifts within the same 'real boundary' token).
